question: Should OpenClaw core own a durable Pi-to-Review-to-local-Git-promotion orchestration subsystem and its contracts runtime, or should this workflow remain outside core behind an existing extension/service boundary?
rationale: The branch adds a new persistent workflow, local service protocol, and promotion capability rather than fixing a documented core contract; source review alone cannot decide the intended permanent owner boundary.

options.title: Decline the core subsystem
options.body: Keep orchestration and contracts in the owning platform/service repository or an external integration, leaving OpenClaw core unchanged.

options.title: Sponsor a bounded core seam
options.body: Approve a narrowly defined generic core API first, then require a follow-up implementation that avoids service-specific policy and uses reviewed source-owned contracts.

options.title: Adopt this direction
options.body: Explicitly accept Core ownership, authorize the dependency/security changes, and require complete fresh-install, upgrade, and real behavior proof before merge.

recommendation.title: Decline the core subsystem
recommendation.body: Keep orchestration and contracts in the owning platform/service repository or an external integration, leaving OpenClaw core unchanged.

likelyOwner.reason: A repository owner for the existing TaskFlow and core architecture boundary must identify the intended long-term owner before this capability can be accepted.
